# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可

1	\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	Multi-turn dialogue is the dominant mode of interaction with large language models (LLMs), and system prompts that specify task goals form the foundation of instruction following. As conversations grow longer, however, models progressively lose track of these goal specifications. \citet{dongre2026attention} quantified this degradation across 12 models: the Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR), which measures how much attention the model allocates to goal tokens in the system prompt, declines by 27--48\% between early and mid-conversation turns. We replicate and extend this finding on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, observing a 70.8\% relative decline in GAR from 0.0418 at turn~1 to 0.0122 at mid-conversation. We attribute the steeper decline partly to our use of last-token GAR, which captures summary-position attention more sensitively than the all-token average of \citet{dongre2026attention}, and partly to Qwen-2.5-7B's stronger instruction-following fidelity in early turns. This attention decay represents a systematic failure of multi-turn models to maintain task coherence, and it grows worse with each additional turn.
4	
5	A striking aspect of this degradation is what it does \emph{not} affect. \citet{dongre2026attention} showed that goal-relevant information persists in the residual stream throughout the conversation: linear discriminant analysis probes recover goal content with AUC\,=\,0.98 even at late turns where attention to goal tokens has collapsed. The information is present in the hidden states, but the attention mechanism fails to route it toward the output computation. This dissociation between information availability and information utilization suggests a natural intervention point.
6	
7	If the residual stream already carries goal information, a learnable gate on the residual pathway could amplify or attenuate layer contributions to recover goal attention. This reasoning motivates ThreadGate, which modulates each residual update with a content-and-turn-conditioned MLP gate: $x_{l+1} = x_l + g_l \cdot f_l(x_l)$, where $g_l$ is produced by a two-layer network conditioned on the hidden state and turn features, inspired by the residual scaling idea of ReZero \citep{bachlechner2021rezero}.
8	
9	\begin{figure*}[t]
10	  \centering
11	  \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig1_overview.pdf}
12	  \caption{Overview of ThreadGate and its failure mode. (Left) ThreadGate adds per-layer content-and-turn-conditioned MLP gates to the residual stream, trained jointly with an auxiliary GAR loss that targets goal attention. (Right) Under teacher-forced evaluation, GAR-ours reaches 0.50 across all fine-tuned variants; under autoregressive generation, it drops to 0.019--0.064, an 8--17$\times$ gap. Turn-conditioned gating (ThreadGate) significantly outperforms LoRA-only ($p$\,=\,0.004) but the residual gap remains large (7.8$\times$).}
13	  \label{fig:overview}
14	\end{figure*}
15	
16	We train ThreadGate jointly with NTP, an auxiliary GAR loss ($\tau\!=\!0.5$), and a gate diversity regularizer; the MSE formulation emerged from seven iterations across four loss families (\S\ref{sec:loss}). A five-way controlled comparison---ThreadGate, +PCGrad, Uniform Gate, LoRA-only, Base---isolates turn conditioning, gating mechanism, gradient conflict, and fine-tuning as factors (\S\ref{sec:comparison-design}). Training succeeds (teacher-forced GAR-ours\,=\,0.50), but autoregressive GAR drops to 0.019--0.064, an 8--17$\times$ gap. Turn-conditioned gating significantly outperforms LoRA-only ($p$\,=\,0.004) yet the residual gap remains large (7.8$\times$); PCGrad-based gradient surgery \citep{yu2020pcgrad} rules out direction conflict. These contrasts converge on exposure bias \citep{bengio2015scheduled}: attention patterns optimized under teacher-forced prefixes do not transfer to model-generated text (Figure~\ref{fig:overview}). Inference-time steering ($\beta$\,=\,5) recovers GAR to 0.727, and scheduled sampling compresses the gap to 1.44$\times$ with no PPL cost (single seed; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
17	
18	Our contributions: (1)~a diagnostic framework comprising a five-way controlled comparison, PCGrad-based causal exclusion, and per-layer gradient analysis that together identify exposure bias as the failure mechanism (\S\ref{sec:analysis}); (2)~an empirical characterization showing exposure bias selectively destroys auxiliary attention losses (8--17$\times$ gap on Qwen-2.5-7B, 27$\times$ on Llama-3.1-8B) while NTP self-recovers \citep{he2019exposure}, with scheduled sampling compressing the gap from 7.8$\times$ to 1.44$\times$; (3)~constructive evidence via inference-time steering that attention misallocation---not representation degradation---is the proximal cause (\S\ref{subsec:steering}); (4)~a principled negative baseline: seven loss configurations across four families, of which only MSE converges (\S\ref{sec:loss}).

Fine-tuned to allocate 50\% of its attention to system-prompt goals (GAR\,=\,0.50 under teacher forcing), Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct retains only GAR\,=\,0.064 under autoregressive generation---an 8$\times$ collapse that widens to 27$\times$ on Llama-3.1-8B. No work examines how per-layer transformer behavior varies across conversation turns (the \emph{turn$\times$depth} gap). Existing remediations---split-softmax \citep{li2024measuring}, StreamingLLM \citep{xiao2024streaming}, gated attention \citep{qiu2025gated}---operate at inference time or are turn-agnostic; \emph{training-time} multi-turn attention optimization is unexplored. And classical exposure bias mitigation \citep{bengio2015scheduled,lamb2016professor} targets RNN sequence generation; no \emph{multi-turn transformer equivalent} exists.

ThreadGate addresses these gaps with per-layer content-and-turn-conditioned MLP gates on the residual stream: $x_{l+1} = x_l + g_l \cdot f_l(x_l)$, where $g_l$ is a two-layer network conditioned on hidden states and turn position. A five-way controlled comparison---ThreadGate, +PCGrad, Uniform Gate, LoRA-only, Base---isolates turn conditioning, gating, gradient conflict, and fine-tuning (\S\ref{sec:comparison-design}), where each adjacent pair kills exactly one alternative hypothesis.

lines: -Multi-turn dialogue is the dominant mode of interaction with large language models (LLMs), and system prompts that specify task goals form the foundation of instruction following. As conversations grow longer, however, models progressively lose track of these goal specifications. \citet{dongre2026attention} quantified this degradation across 12 models: the Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR), which measures how much attention the model allocates to goal tokens in the system prompt, declines by 27--48\% between early and mid-conversation turns. We replicate and extend this finding on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, observing a 70.8\% relative decline in GAR from 0.0418 at turn~1 to 0.0122 at mid-conversation. We attribute the steeper decline partly to our use of last-token GAR, which captures summary-position attention more sensitively than the all-token average of \citet{dongre2026attention}, and partly to Qwen-2.5-7B's stronger instruction-following fidelity in early turns. This attention decay represents a systematic failure of multi-turn models to maintain task coherence, and it grows worse with each additional turn.

+Fine-tuned to allocate 50\% of its attention to system-prompt goals (GAR\,=\,0.50 under teacher forcing), Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct retains only GAR\,=\,0.064 under autoregressive generation---an 8$\times$ collapse that widens to 27$\times$ on Llama-3.1-8B. This paper traces the failure to exposure bias \citep{bengio2015scheduled}: attention patterns optimized under teacher-forced prefixes do not transfer to model-generated text, even when next-token prediction (NTP) remains robust.

-A striking aspect of this degradation is what it does \emph{not} affect. \citet{dongre2026attention} showed that goal-relevant information persists in the residual stream throughout the conversation: linear discriminant analysis probes recover goal content with AUC\,=\,0.98 even at late turns where attention to goal tokens has collapsed. The information is present in the hidden states, but the attention mechanism fails to route it toward the output computation. This dissociation between information availability and information utilization suggests a natural intervention point.

\paragraph{Attention manipulation.}
StreamingLLM \citep{xiao2024streaming} identified attention sinks and proposed anchor token retention; \citet{hsieh2024found} showed positional bias against middle-positioned information; \citet{qiu2025gated} replaced softmax with a learned gate for sparse attention; Rhea \citep{hong2025rhea} introduces role-aware episodic attention for multi-turn dialogue. Subsequent work targets computational efficiency: LayerDrop \citep{fan2020layerdrop}, Mixture-of-Depths \citep{raposo2024mixture}, FlexiDepth \citep{luo2025flexidepth}, and CALM \citep{schuster2022calm}. \citet{gromov2024unreasonable} showed that removing up to half a model's layers preserves most capability, paralleling our finding that LoRA-only matches all gating variants. ThreadGate applies residual gating to a different objective: recovering attention patterns in multi-turn dialogue.

+StreamingLLM \citep{xiao2024streaming} identified attention sinks and proposed anchor token retention; \citet{hsieh2024found} showed positional bias against middle-positioned information; Rhea \citep{hong2025rhea} introduces role-aware episodic attention for multi-turn dialogue. PASTA \citep{zhang2024tell} steers attention post-hoc by reweighting a subset of attention heads; our $\beta$-steering applies a simpler additive bias to all layers but serves a diagnostic purpose. These approaches intervene inside the attention mechanism, while ThreadGate operates on the residual stream.

+Most relevant to our architecture is Gated Attention \citep{qiu2025gated}, which places a head-specific sigmoid gate after scaled dot-product attention, breaking the $W_V \cdot W_O$ low-rank bottleneck with query-dependent sparsity. Trained at scale (15B MoE, 3.5T tokens), it achieves PPL $-$0.265, MMLU $+$2.03, and reduces first-token attention concentration from 46.7\% to 4.8\% with $<$2\% overhead. The key distinction is granularity: their gate operates per-head within a single forward pass (turn-agnostic), while ThreadGate conditions on turn position to modulate per-layer residual contributions across conversation turns. Our results demonstrate that even with turn conditioning, training-time attention objectives face a fundamental exposure bias barrier that head-level gating does not address because it never targets an auxiliary attention distribution.

GradNorm \citep{chen2018gradnorm}, PCGrad \citep{yu2020pcgrad}, CAGrad \citep{liu2021cagrad}, and Nash-MTL \citep{navon2022nash} treat gradient conflict between competing losses as a root cause to be resolved through better optimization. We repurpose PCGrad as a diagnostic tool: eliminating directional conflict between NTP and GAR gradients does not improve GAR convergence. Gradient conflict is a symptom rather than the cause.

input.old_string: Multi-turn dialogue with LLMs suffers from progressive attention decay toward system-prompt goal tokens. On Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, the Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR) declines 70.8\% between early and mid-conversation turns, yet linear probes recover goal content from the residual stream (AUC\,=\,0.98). We introduce ThreadGate, per-layer content-and-turn-conditioned MLP gates trained jointly with next-token prediction and an auxiliary GAR loss. A five-way controlled comparison shows training succeeds (teacher-forced GAR\,=\,0.50) but autoregressive GAR collapses to 0.019--0.064, an 8--17$\times$ gap; turn-conditioned gating significantly outperforms LoRA-only ($p$\,=\,0.004) but the residual gap remains large (7.8$\times$), and PCGrad excludes gradient conflict. The failure traces to exposure bias: attention patterns learned under teacher-forced prefixes do not transfer to model-generated text. Steering ($\beta$\,=\,5) recovers GAR to 0.727 and scheduled sampling compresses the gap to 1.44$\times$ (single seed); cross-model evaluation on Llama-3.1-8B confirms the gap (27$\times$ by median). These findings characterize how exposure bias selectively destroys auxiliary attention losses while leaving the primary NTP objective robust.
input.new_string: Fine-tuned to allocate 50\% of attention to system-prompt goals (GAR\,=\,0.50 under teacher forcing), Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct retains only GAR\,=\,0.064 under autoregressive generation---an 8$\times$ collapse. We trace this failure to exposure bias: attention patterns optimized under teacher-forced prefixes do not transfer to model-generated text. ThreadGate, per-layer content-and-turn-conditioned MLP gates trained with an auxiliary GAR loss, provides a controlled testbed. A five-way comparison isolates turn conditioning, gating, gradient conflict, and fine-tuning; each pair kills one hypothesis. Gating outperforms LoRA-only ($p$\,=\,0.004) but the gap remains 7.8$\times$; PCGrad eliminates gradient conflict but \emph{worsens} AR GAR ($p$\,=\,0.002), ruling out the most intuitive failure mechanism by \emph{modus tollens}. Steering ($\beta$\,=\,5) recovers GAR to 0.727; scheduled sampling compresses the gap to 1.44$\times$ (single seed). Cross-model evaluation on Llama-3.1-8B confirms a 27$\times$ gap. These findings establish that exposure bias selectively destroys auxiliary attention losses while NTP self-recovers---a failure mode with no prior multi-turn transformer characterization.

ThreadGate adds per-layer gated MLP networks with an auxiliary GAR loss; training succeeds (TF GAR\,=\,0.50) but autoregressive GAR collapses 8--17$\times$ on Qwen-2.5-7B (27$\times$ on Llama-3.1-8B). Gating provides modest improvement over LoRA-only ($p$\,=\,0.004) but is insufficient to close the gap. Steering ($\beta$\,=\,5, GAR 0.727) and scheduled sampling (gap 7.8$\times$$\to$1.44$\times$; single seed) implicate attention misallocation as the proximal cause.

A figure taking 6 inches leaves only 3.5 inches for text, and if the remaining text doesn't fill that space, we get whitespace.
